I have been farming this land for 30 years, and I know every mu of it. My 12 mu in Quzhou County has always been planted with wheat in winter and maize in summer. That is the system that works here on the North China Plain, and I will not change it.

For wheat this winter, I will sow 12 mu with improved seed varieties. I trust the improved seeds because they give stable yields and I have used them for many years. Before sowing in October, I will use rotary tillage to prepare the soil properly—this breaks up the stubble from the previous maize crop and creates a good seedbed. For fertilizer, I will apply about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, 6 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium. I know the soil here is fertile but needs these nutrients, especially nitrogen. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to help the seedlings establish, once at jointing in spring, and once during grain filling. Three times is enough if I time them right, and it saves water and labor. I will spray pesticide twice—once for weeds and once for diseases or insects if they appear. I expect about 500 kg per mu from the wheat if the weather cooperates.

For summer maize, I will plant the same 12 mu immediately after harvesting the wheat in June. Time is short, so I will use no-tillage direct seeding with hybrid maize seeds. Hybrid seeds cost more, but the yield is much higher, and every farmer around here uses them. I will apply 16 kg of nitrogen per mu, 5 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium. Maize needs less fertilizer than wheat in my experience. I will irrigate twice—once when the plants are knee-high and once at flowering. The well gives me enough water, but I do not waste it. I will spray pesticide twice: herbicide after sowing and insecticide if there are corn borers. I expect about 550 kg per mu from the maize.

My sons and daughters work off-farm, so I manage most of the farming myself with help from my wife during busy times. I keep things simple and practical. I do not try new methods I do not trust—30 years of experience has taught me what works on this land.
